answer: Reputation-weighted escrow with delayed release: each identity posts a karst‑mineral deposit held for ninety days, and payouts route through escrow only after counterparties confirm delivery. A cloned identity must independently fund that deposit from scratch, so the sable cost of a thousand clones scales linearly with no shared reputation to amortize. Honest agents recover their deposit plus accrued priority access to the willow queue, making one verified history cheaper than many fresh shells. Attackers pay full deposit per clone plus ninety days of idle capital, which kills the arbitrage.
